speaker: ALEX
text: Our second story. The IMF — 191 member countries, decades of managing global debt and financial crises — is now telling those countries to regulate AI faster. Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva delivered that warning in Singapore on October 7th, ahead of IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok next week.

speaker: RUFUS
text: The thing to watch next week is Bangkok. If Georgieva's October 7th language appears in the official communiqué from the IMF-World Bank meetings, AI regulation moves from a speech to a shared institutional position across 191 member countries. That's the signal worth tracking.

speaker: JAMIE
text: That's what "privilege creep" means in practice. The agent doesn't ask for more access — it just has more than it uses, and eventually something exercises it.

speaker: RUFUS
text: Picture the Sands Expo in Singapore — a conference venue that has hosted more urgent global warnings than most cities host weather events. Georgieva is at a podium with Bangkok and 191 country delegations waiting in the wings. She links AI not to innovation policy but to debt sustainability and inequality. That framing is deliberate.
